name: Reykjadalur hot river
region: Hengill area, above Hveragerði, south Iceland
why: An hour up a steaming green valley to a warm river where you bathe in the open, with changing screens on the boardwalk.
book: Free walk, paid parking at the trailhead north of Hveragerði. The Environment Agency closes the path in wet spring weeks to save it: check before you go.
water: None to drink on the way: carry it. The river is warm, not drinking water.
dangers: Boiling springs and mud pots beside the path: never step off it, the ground can be a thin crust.
The water is hotter upstream: test it before you get in, move downstream to cool down.
turnaround: Back down before dark: the path is unlit and slippery when frozen.

points.name: Reykjadalur trailhead, Hveragerði
points.note: The car park and café at the end of the road north of town; the path climbs the first hill at once.

points.name: Djúpagilsfoss and the steaming valley
points.note: Over the ridge the valley opens, green and steaming, with the Djúpagil waterfall on the left.

points.name: Reykjadalsá bathing boardwalk
points.note: The wooden boardwalk with screens along the warm river; the best water is where a hot spring joins it.
